S.FORM: Varean sasa mun nēk, jujun̄ ga rēē.
S.TRANSL: Un grand merci à toi, chef !
{Thank you very much, sir.

S.FORM: Muk mula tay ususraa ne, na ga mērēs ga la woy mula.
S.TRANSL: J’ai encore une autre histoire, que je voudrais raconter.
I have another story which I’d like to tell you.}

S.FORM: Tay vōnō nēy mō saa lē vōnō won, gatav, m̄o.
S.TRANSL: Il était une fois un village, autrefois, au milieu de la forêt.
Once upon a time, people were living in the forest – a long time ago.

S.FORM: Nēy mō saa van van va– van, jujun̄ mō mat ni mō mat, ni mō mat vavavan –
S.TRANSL: One day, people began to die, one after the other.

S.FORM: Raqa tuwa, m̄arat tuwa.
S.TRANSL: Then there was a couple – a woman and a man.

S.FORM: Nōrō mō saa van van van van, mon m̄arat mō mat vutaa ni.
S.TRANSL: They lived together for a while, until one day her husband passed away.

S.FORM: Alē, mon raqa ne taqan iē. Raqa nan̄ ni m-saa woy m̄aasen.
S.TRANSL: But this woman was pregnant, and she now had to live on her own.

S.FORM: Ni m-tuy saa ni m-gis mon key. Key mogon ni mō mēnēē.
S.TRANSL: One day she took hold of her walking stick – one she had enchanted.

S.FORM: Ni m-van ma, tay vat tē tuy ti lē mataale.
S.TRANSL: She walked around, and found a rock standing alongside the road.

S.FORM: Ni tē rara ti, ni tē tēw vat ne mē mon key.
S.TRANSL: With tears in her eyes, she began to poke the rock with her magic stick.

S.FORM: Tēw tēw tēw tēw vat vavavan, qayn̄ēn mō rēē.
S.TRANSL: And as she poked the rock again and again, suddenly a large cave formed in it.

S.FORM: Mon vuvuy gaiv, mon vuvuy mō jay jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: The woman was homeless – as her house had decayed.

S.FORM: Alē ni m-tēw vat van va– van, qayn̄ēn mō rēē; mō ris mon vuvuy mē.
S.TRANSL: And so she poked the rock on and on, which created a large cavity; and this became her new home.

S.FORM: Ti ni m-gis iē rowol lē vat ne, ni m-saa iē. 🌿
S.TRANSL: Without further ado, she entered the cave and settled in it. 🌿

S.FORM: Saa van van vavavan, ni m-la putē, m̄arat.
S.TRANSL: She stayed there for some time, and finally gave birth to her child, a boy.

S.FORM: Alē, putē m̄arat ne, gēngēn gaiv jēn raqa ne, ni tē vēn̄ēn putē ne mēn wa palak a men ti.
S.TRANSL: But then, the woman had no food to give to her little boy; she could only feed him with wild figs, when she found some that were ripe enough.

S.FORM: Mon putē ga mērēs t-gēngēn, ni ga rowol, van ēm palak, wa palak ga men, sugēn lē gat, van mē ma, vēn̄ēn nōtōn mē.
S.TRANSL: Every time her baby wanted to eat, she would go out and look for wild figs; when she found a ripe one she would put it in her basket, and bring it back to feed her child.

S.FORM: Gēngēn mu putē ne, wa palak vatwal woy.
S.TRANSL: Often she had no other food for her baby, than just a single wild fig.

S.FORM: Ni tē ēs woy mē sōsōn viven ti; la gēngēn, palak, palak ga men. 🌿
S.TRANSL: He had nothing more to survive than his mother’s milk, and a ripe fig for food. 🌿

S.FORM: Nōrō m-saa van van va– van, putē m̄arat ne m-rēē, vit mun viven ron̄ “Evō!” Ron̄ “A?” Ron̄ “Na ga mērēs nēk a tusun̄ muk vus. Nēk a tusun̄ muk tay vus.”
S.TRANSL: So that’s how they lived together for several years. One day, as the boy had grown up, he asked his mother “Mum!” – “Yes?” she said, – “I’d like you to make me a bow. Please make me a bow.”

S.FORM: Viven ron̄ “O, nutuk! Na gatē mērēs wōs tusun̄ mon̄ vus nan̄ suy na n-raqa.”
S.TRANSL: – “Oh boy!” replied his mother. “I’m not going to make you a bow, I’m a woman!”

S.FORM: Alē, nōtōn vit ron̄ “Na nawon woy, evō! Taltal woy nēk ōl tē wokem vēlē wōs, wokem parakōt woy mun na. Na ga mērēs vinē nēy qilis, nōtam.”
S.TRANSL: – “It doesn’t matter, Mum!” he replied. “It’s alright if it’s not perfect, just make me an ordinary bow. I just want to go and hunt lizards outside.”

S.FORM: Alē, viven gis iē, tusun̄ tay vus mun ni.
S.TRANSL: So his mother set off to make a bow for him.

S.FORM: Gis iē, mō la tuli jajun̄, tuli woy. Ni m-ris wae mē.
S.TRANSL: Then she found some midribs of sago leaves – just the midrib – and made arrows out of them.

S.FORM: (M̄o, ma vak jēk, wae gaiv.)
S.TRANSL: (In the olden days, we had no metal arrows.)

S.FORM: Ni m-la woy tultuli jajun̄, ni m-sēp pas woy, vivis woy gapēnis mogon, vaga mon vus, la mun ni nirō. 🌿
S.TRANSL: So she found these midribs of sago leaves, cut them the right size, and fastened their points. Then she bent the bow and gave it to him, with two arrows. 🌿

S.FORM: Matvas nan̄ ni ga mamat, ni van nōtam, ni vinē qilis, jalgēt mon vuvuy tē pira ka mē ti.
S.TRANSL: As he woke up the next morning, he went outside, and began to shoot small lizards; he went on playing like that around his house.

S.FORM: Vavavan, viven ron̄ “Nutuk, na tē vay nēk ti, nēk ōl pipira olbaōt m̄ay nan̄, nēk mētē van ley ras.”
S.TRANSL: At some point, his mother told him: “My son, I’m warning you: if you wander around like that, make sure you don’t go too far.”

S.FORM: Nōtōn ron̄ “Suy sa, evō?” Ron̄ “Óòǒ, suy Tamat Gēngēn iē, saa tē vak nan̄. Nōtnōtōn nivat. Nēy tē van kēlkēl ti, tē ran̄ putē ti, tē la mun viven ti, ni tē gēn ti.”
S.TRANSL: “Why, Mum?” he asked. – “Because there’s an Ogress living over there. She has four sons who walk around, kidnap children, and bring them to their Ogress mother for her dinner.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “M̄arē wujek.”, ron̄ “Ni ras, le…?”
S.TRANSL: – “Oh, really?” – and he added “But does she live far away from here?”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Óòǒ, tē ras sasa wōs. Maate nan̄ Tamat Gēngēn.”
S.TRANSL: – “No no” she replied, “not too far. But that old witch is an Ogress.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Ga wē, evō! Nēk tē suy woy na ti. Qōn̄ tuwa, na ga van suy Tamat Gēngēn.”
S.TRANSL: – “That’s fine, Mum! You can trust me. One of these days, I’ll go and meet that Ogress.”

S.FORM: Viven ron̄ “Sōw, nutuk! Na tē rara woy nēk ti mētē van ley, na woy m̄aasēk, ka nēk a van jēn na Tamat Gēngēn ga ēl nēk, na ga saa woy m̄aasēk, mamrōs woy.”
S.TRANSL: – “Please, my son! I’m imploring you, please, don’t go! Don’t leave me alone! If you go there, the Ogress will find you, and I’ll end up all alone and miserable.”

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ “Taltal woy, evō! Nēk tē suy woy na ti, qōn̄ tuwa na ga van.”
S.TRANSL: – “Don’t worry, Mum! Just trust me. One day I’ll go.”

S.FORM: Van va– van, putē nan̄ sa ni m-rēē, ni ron̄ “Evō, talōw na ga van.”
S.TRANSL: Time went by, and the little boy grew bigger. One day he said “Mum! Tomorrow is the day.”

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ “O, nutuk, na tē ukaa wōs nēk.
S.TRANSL: – “No my son”, she replied, “I won’t allow you.”

S.FORM: – Suy sa? – Suy nēk mētē van, ni mtē gēn mamat nēk jēn na!
S.TRANSL: – “Why?” – “Because if you go, she’ll eat you alive, and I’ll lose you!”

S.FORM: – O, taltal woy, na ga van vatnasē. Ni ōl gēn na, ga wē, ni ōl tē gēn wōs na, na ga van lōk ma suy nēk.” 🌿
S.TRANSL: – “No no, stop worrying!” he said. “Let me give it a try. If she eats me, well, so be it; but if she doesn’t, I promise I’ll come back to you.” 🌿

S.FORM: Nōrō m-saa van van va– van, qōn̄ tuwa, ni mō gis mon vus, mata vinvinē, ni van.
S.TRANSL: They stayed together for a while, but eventually came the day when he grabbed his bow and arrows, and left.

S.FORM: Van van van, ni van ma suy Tamat Gēngēn ne, tē on ti le vuvuy.
S.TRANSL: He walked all the way until he got to the Ogress, who was lying in her house.

S.FORM: Tamat Gēngēn ne mō ron̄ sē lēn̄ tē van ma. Lēn̄ nan̄ ga maymay ga maymay tam̄ay lēn̄vus!
S.TRANSL: The Ogress felt like the wind was rising. It grew stronger and stronger, it was like a hurricane!

S.FORM: Tepel tē jēv lē tavtēn, jarok tē kal ti meken, tē lan̄ vuvuy ti.
S.TRANSL: Basket dishes fell on the floor, cooking leaves rose up in the air, even the house was being lifted up!

S.FORM: Vuvuy ga mērēs a kamaot, maate mō gis iē waa ti lē num.
S.TRANSL: When she saw her house ready to be blown away, the old witch jumped into her oven pit.

S.FORM: Matvut.
S.TRANSL: She was terrified.

S.FORM: Putē m-row tuy le mataalol.
S.TRANSL: The boy landed right on her doorstep.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Ōōy!” Maate ron̄ “Ōy!”
S.TRANSL: “Hey!” he said. – “Hey!” answered the witch.

S.FORM: Maate tē on ti lē num, ni m-suruu ni mēn jarok, javay; ni ron̄ –
S.TRANSL: She was hiding in her oven pit, her head covered with cooking leaves of burao.

S.FORM: Vurus maate ron̄ “Maate!” Ron̄ “Oo? – Mon̄ gēngēn iē?”
S.TRANSL: He called her again “Hey, old witch!” – “Yes?” – “Got some food?”

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ “Mm, muk gēngēn iē. – La ma jōrō gēn!”
S.TRANSL: – “Uh, yes, sure, I have food.”– “Bring it on,” he said, “let’s eat together!”

S.FORM: Maate mō gēn woy ga varii, ni ni m-gēn ga rēē.
S.TRANSL: The old woman ate just a little, and he ate lots.

S.FORM: Alē ni m-vurus mula pē.
S.TRANSL: And then he asked her for water.

S.FORM: “Non̄ pē iē? – Mm! – La ma jōrō un!”
S.TRANSL: “Got some water?” – “Yes!” – “Bring it on, let’s share it!”

S.FORM: Maate nan̄ mō un pas pē, nōtōn ni un.
S.TRANSL: The old woman drank some, and so did the boy.

S.FORM: Pas, ni van jēn ni, rurus ni roy le mataalol. Ni van jēn ni. Vēsēj kal ti le mataalol, to vutaa ni.
S.TRANSL: And then it was time to leave. He dragged her out to the doorway, tied her up above the doorway, and left her there hanging as he walked away from her.

S.FORM: Ni van lōk suy viven. Viven tē saa ti, ni vat mula ma.
S.TRANSL: He went back to his mother’s. At last she was able to see him again!

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ “Evō! Nēk mō vit suy Tamat Gēngēn, ni tē gēn wōs na! Ka ni matvut woy na! Ti ni m-to lē num! Rurus ni ma sēj ni ti le mataalol.” 🌿
S.TRANSL: “Mum,” he said, “You warned me against the Ogress, but she didn’t eat me. In fact she was even scared of me! She jumped in her oven pit! And then I hung her up above the doorway.” 🌿

S.FORM: Nōtnōtōn van ma van ma van ma, jurun̄ saa le mataalol, viverō tē taka ti / viven tēlēy.
S.TRANSL: Over there, the sons of the Ogress were on their way back home. Suddenly they looked up above the door, and saw their mother hanging from there.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “O! Isē mō jaw vivej m̄ay ne? Gēj a van saa, ga vurus sē vivej, sa m-jaw ni.”
S.TRANSL: “Oh!” they said, “Who did that to our mother? Hurry up, let’s ask her who did that!”

S.FORM: Van saa, vurus maate ron̄ “Evō! Nēk tē saa ti, sē m-sēj nēk lē mataalol m̄ay ne?”
S.TRANSL: They ran up, and ask their old mother “Mum! Who tied you up to the door and left you hanging like that?”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “O, tēlēy nutnutuk! Tay putē ga varii m-van ma ne, ni m-gal na suy gēngēn, suy pē, ni m-sugēn karkaran̄kē [polpolon̄ta] na, ni m-vay na suy gēngēn mēn pē, ni tē jēv jēn lē vēlēk ti.
S.TRANSL: – “Oh my children! It’s a small boy who came here, and lured me into eating and drinking; he was stuffing me like crazy! He asked me for food and water, and forced it into my mouth!

S.FORM: Ni m-gis iē, rurus na ti lē mataalol, lēē rakat ti lē mataalol, to jēn na.”
S.TRANSL: And then suddenly he dragged me all the way to the doorway, tied me up above the door, and he walked away!”

S.FORM: “O, ga wē!” (Tēlēy putputē nan̄, tēlēy pul vat.) “Ga wē, talōw, pul tēl ga van lē naw, tuwa ga saa. Suy ni ga gēn putē ga varii nan̄.” 🌿
S.TRANSL: – “Alright!” they said. (Remember she had four children.) “Tomorrow, only three of us will go down to the sea, but one will stay here. He’ll just wolf that small boy down!” 🌿

S.FORM: Talōw matvas, pul tēl mō van lē naw, tuwa mō saa.
S.TRANSL: So the next morning, three of them went to the sea, while one stayed home.

S.FORM: Saa van van van, ni ron̄ “Evō!” Ron̄ “Mm?” Ron̄ “Ni ga van ma qirii, le…?” Ron̄ “Mm!” – “Ni ga van vatēētēē ma, na a gēn ni! Ni ka m-qisgaa nēk nanono.”
S.TRANSL: After a while, he asked “Mother!” – “Yes?” she said, – “Do you think he’ll come today?” – “Yes.” – “I can’t wait! As soon as he comes, I’ll wolf him down! He did you so wrong yesterday…”

S.FORM: Tē garat tēktēqēl lēwon ti, suy putē ne ka ni ga gēn ni.
S.TRANSL: He was gnashing his teeth noisily, impatient to eat the little boy.

S.FORM: Nōrō saa saa saa van van va– van, ni vurus mula viven, ron̄ “Evō, ni ga van ma le ga gasva?”
S.TRANSL: They waited for a long, long time. “Mother!” he asked again, “when do you think he’ll come?”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Asval ti! Na m-ron̄ ka ni van ma, na tak vit jērēs mun nēk.”
S.TRANSL: – “Be patient!” she said. “As soon as I hear him come, I’ll let you know.”

S.FORM: Nōrō m-saa va–van, maate ne ron̄ sē, lēn̄ ti van nok mala ma.
S.TRANSL: After a while, the old witch began to feel the wind again.

S.FORM: Alē, maate ne vit ron̄ “Ni nok mala jek le, nutuk!”
S.TRANSL: “Oh my son!” she said. “Here he comes again!”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Vutwē?” Ron̄ “Ga wē. Ni van ma, na ga gēn ni!”
S.TRANSL: – “Oh really? Perfect! Bring him on, I’ll just eat him up!”

S.FORM: Putē nan̄ gis iē, tuy pēt mataalol, tēlēn̄ jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: The boy quickly went to stand close to the door, hidden from sight.

S.FORM: Mō gis mon wotaray ni ga vus putē ga varii ne.
S.TRANSL: He was holding a club, ready to hit our small boy upon his arrival.

S.FORM: Lēn̄ mō vēē vaa-tuwa ma ga maymay, ga maymay mamaavis ka mamaavis jēn nanono.
S.TRANSL: But the wind grew stronger and stronger – considerably stronger than yesterday.

S.FORM: Ni van sēv nanono, nanono ga varii; qirii ne ga maymay sasa.
S.TRANSL: The hurricane of yesterday was nothing in comparison: the one today was far stronger.

S.FORM: Putē ne gis iē, ni matvut, saa sēw vak lē num ne, suruu ni mēn jarok.
S.TRANSL: Scared to death, the boy jumped in the oven pit, and covered himself with cooking leaves.

S.FORM: Putē ne ni m-row tuy lē mataalol.
S.TRANSL: The other child landed right at the doorway.

S.FORM: Ni vurus maate suy gēngēn, vēn̄ēn mala ni, ron̄ “Non̄ pē iē?” Ron̄ “Mm, iē!”
S.TRANSL: He asked the old witch for food, and fed her again; then he asked “Got any water?” – “Yes!” she replied.

S.FORM: La pē mun ni ni m-un pas, rurus mala maate roy lē mataalol, sēj rakat ni saa lē mataalol. To jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: Once he had had her drink all the water, he dragged the old woman out to the doorway, tied her up above the door – and walked away.

S.FORM: La nōtōn ne tē vus wōs putē ne.
S.TRANSL: Her son didn’t even get a chance to catch the boy!

S.FORM: Ni van lōk. Van lōk vak, vit mun viven ron̄ “Evō! Nēk mō suy woy na na van vaa-rō gēn jek le. La Tamat Gēngēn te gēn wōs na. Suy sa m̄ēē? La talōw, na ga van mula.”
S.TRANSL: So he returned back home. When he arrived, he told his mother “Mum! Even though you forbade me, I’ve been there twice already. Yet that Ogress never ate me! How’s this?! Tomorrow, I’m going there again.”

S.FORM: Viven mō rara woy ni, ron̄ “Sōw nutuk! Nēk van nok vaa-rō, nēk mō ēs nok. Na tē mērēs wōs ka nēk a van mula. Ni ka jaw vaa-tēl ni a gēn nēk.”
S.TRANSL: His mother, in tears, tried to dissuade him: “Oh, my boy! You went there twice, and you survived. But I don’t want to see you go back. If you do once more, she’ll eat you.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Talōw na a van mula, evō.”
S.TRANSL: – “I’ll go again tomorrow, Mum.”

S.FORM: Talōw, ni van mula. 🌿
S.TRANSL: And the next day indeed, he went again. 🌿

S.FORM: Van mula, ni m-jaw jējēm men le qōn̄ nirō.
S.TRANSL: So he went again, and did exactly like the other two days.

S.FORM: Ni vurus mula gēngēn, ron̄ “Gēngēn lē gakul tē taka ti lē gat.”
S.TRANSL: Asked again for food, she answered “There’s some food in that basket up there, that’s hanging from the hook.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “La suy ma jōrō gēn.”
S.TRANSL: – “Alright, let’s eat together!”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Non̄ pē iē?” – “Nōk pē le wetelwa.” – “La ma jōrō un.”
S.TRANSL: “What about water?” he asked. – “There’s some in the calabash.” – “Let’s drink it.”

S.FORM: Alē, maate m-un pas, putē m-un pas, ran̄ rurus ni roy, vēsēj rakat ni, vēsēj le mataalol.
S.TRANSL: So she drank, and he drank, then he dragged her out, and hung her up there above the door.

S.FORM: Ni van lōk jēn ni. Ni van jēn̄ un viven.
S.TRANSL: Walked away again. Went back to his mother.

S.FORM: Viven ron̄ “O nutuk, nēk gasva?” – “Na ga ēs woy! Ni tē gēn wōs na! Nēk mō vit ka Tamat Gēngēn tē gēn jujun̄ ti, la ni tē gēn wōs na, vaa-tēl ēn jēk! Vaa-tuwa ti!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: “My son!” she exclaimed, “what happened?” – “I’m alive! She hasn’t eaten me. You warned me against an Ogress who ate people, but she never ate me. That’s the third time already – let me go once again!” 🌿

S.FORM: Nōtnōtōn kal ma, ēl sē lē mataalol ne, viverō tē taka mula ti, viven tēlēy.
S.TRANSL: Meanwhile, the witch’s boys came back home, looked up at the door, and saw their mother hanging again.

S.FORM: “Auu! Iva nan̄ ka ni m-saa ti ka suy ni ga gēn putē nan̄, ni tē taka ti saa nan̄ lē mataalol. Vivej tē taka nok mala ti. Gasva m̄ēē?”
S.TRANSL: “Good grief! Our brother was supposed to wait for that boy and eat him up; yet here she is again, swinging up there above the doorway. Once again we find our mother hanging and tied up! How is this possible?!”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Ga wē. Talōw vagvagē kēlkimi ga van, na na ga saa. Vagvagē nan̄ talōw le.
S.TRANSL: “Alright,” said one of them. “Tomorrow’s the last chance. The three of you will go out, while I’ll stay here. Tomorrow has to be the last time.

S.FORM: Alē, putē nan̄ van lōk suy viven, le qayn̄ēn vat. Talōw jēk, vagvagē van, nēy ka pul vat woy. Ga wē, talōw, kēlkimi ga van, na ga saa. Na ga saa na a gēn putē nan̄.”
S.TRANSL: Right now, that boy is back with his mother, in his cave. But tomorrow, well, there are four of us; the three of you can go, but I’ll stay here. I’ll stay here and gulp him down.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Ga wē, talōw nan̄, nēk tak gēn. Kēlkama mō saa nok, mērēn nitēl kēlkama tē matvut ti. Kama tē jaw wōs. Ga wē, nēk talōw nan̄ vagvagē vaa-vat.” 🌿
S.TRANSL: – “Alright,” they replied. “Tomorrow is your turn. The three of us, we stayed here for these three days, but we all felt terrified, so nobody did anything. Alright, tomorrow will be the fourth and last chance.” 🌿

S.FORM: Talōw matvas, putē vagvagē ne van.
S.TRANSL: So the next morning, our boy set off for the last time.

S.FORM: Van mula ma, gis mula mon vus. Van ma, vutuy ti lē mataalol.
S.TRANSL: {This time, he had taken his bow. When he arrived, he leaned it against the doorstep.}

S.FORM: Rowol saa, vay mula maate ne jēn le vuvuy.
S.TRANSL: He went in, and asked the old woman to come out.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Gan̄ gēngēn meleti?”
S.TRANSL: “Got some food left?” he asked.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Mm, gēk gēngēn iē.” – “La ma jōrō gēn!”
S.TRANSL: – “Yes I have some food.” – “Let’s eat it!”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Non̄ pē meleti?”
S.TRANSL: “Got some water left?”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Mm, nōk pē meleti. Pē ne lē wetelwa.”
S.TRANSL: – “Yes I have water. It’s in the calabash.”

S.FORM: (M̄o, tē tav pē ti lē wetelwa. Noknok ne, tē tav ti lē potel; la m̄o, tē tav naw / tē tav pē ti lē wetelwa.)
S.TRANSL: (In the olden days, people would carry water in calabashes. Nowadays, we use bottles; but before that, it used to be calabashes.)

S.FORM: Vēn̄ēn toktok pas mula maate ne, la pas pē mun ni, rurus mula ni roy, vēsēj rakat ni saa lē mataalol. To jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: {Again he stuffed the old witch with food, gave her water, dragged her out, and hung her up above the doorway. Then walked away.

S.FORM: Tēlēy putē m-kal ma, jurun̄ sē saa nan̄ maate tē taka ti.
S.TRANSL: As her three sons returned home, they caught sight of their old mother hanging from above.

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Óòǒ! Ava! Iva nan̄ ni m-saa ti suy ni ga gēn putē nan̄, vivej tē taka ti lē mataalol. Gasva m̄ēē?” 🌿
S.TRANSL: “Oh no, man! Our brother was supposed to wait for that boy and eat him up; yet here’s our mother, swinging up there above the doorway. How is this just possible?!” 🌿

S.FORM: Ni m-kal ma nan̄, saa sēw vak lē num; gis mon wotaray, putē ga varii nan̄ ni ka mō wata lē vat ne.
S.TRANSL: And then he came back! She went down to hide in the oven pit. This time he was holding a club – that little boy who was born on a rock.

S.FORM: Vus maate!
S.TRANSL: He killed the Ogress!

S.FORM: Jon̄ jara tē vak lē qōtōn ne.
S.TRANSL: Then he began smearing his own head with her blood.

S.FORM: Alē, ni van lōk jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: And he went away.

S.FORM: “Vagvagē talōw, na ga van ma vagvagē!”
S.TRANSL: “Alright, he thought, tomorrow will be the last time. I’ll come back for the last time.”

S.FORM: Talōw matvas, ni van ma.
S.TRANSL: And the next morning, he came back.

S.FORM: Ni m-la mula gēngēn, vēn̄ēn pas mula maate, vēn̄ēn ni, un pas pē, un pas pē –
S.TRANSL: He brought together food again, force-fed the Ogress again, got her to drink water, lots of water –}

S.FORM: Vēsēj ti lē mataalol ne, ni m-gis mon wotaray, waa vak lē num, vus maate ne, jon̄ jarēn ti lē qōtōn.
S.TRANSL: He hung her above the door, seized his club, and suddenly he killed the Ogress! Once he had killed her, he began smearing his own head with her blood.

S.FORM: Ni vit mun viven ron̄ “Evō! Talōw matvas, nēk a van ti lē kērē pē, lē mēlēs pē, lē kērē pē. Nēk a ēl woy jarik. Ka jarik mō lat ma, nan̄ ēn na m-mat. Ka jarik ōl gaiv, na tē mat wōs.”
S.TRANSL: [Earlier on, he had] said to his own mother: “Mother! Tomorrow morning, you will walk down to the river end. Watch out for my blood. If you see my blood flow down, this will mean I’ll be dead. If you see no blood, then I won’t be dead.”

S.FORM: E lē matvas, viven tuy jēn lē vēy, van ti lē kērē pē, saa tēgēy jarēn.
S.TRANSL: So that morning, as soon as she rose from her bed, his mother went to the river end, and sat there watching out for the blood.

S.FORM: Saa van va– van, putē ne vus pas nēy wō Tamat Gēngēn ne, jon̄ pas jarēy tē vak lē qōtōn ne.
S.TRANSL: While she sat there waiting, the boy had killed the Ogress and her four sons, and was covering his own head with their blood.

S.FORM: Ni van ma lē mēlēs pē, row saa ti lē mēlēs pē, jara van jēn ni.
S.TRANSL: He walked to the river, and let himself float all the way downhill, his body dripping with blood.

S.FORM: Alē, viven tē saa ti lē kērē pē. Ēl sē tē woy nōtōn tē sala ma, jara tē van ma.
S.TRANSL: Sitting by the river, his mother suddenly caught sight of her son floating on the water, followed by a long trail of blood.

S.FORM: Viven mō rara ron̄ “A! Nutuk mō mat! Jarēn mō van ma!”
S.TRANSL: “Alas!” she cried, “My son is dead! He is covered in blood!”

S.FORM: Ni m-ēl sē tē sala ma, valrēē mēn jarēn.
S.TRANSL: She was watching him come closer, following the bloody river.

S.FORM: Pē tē ran̄ ni ma. Van ma van ma van ma, jēn̄ wōn viven ne.
S.TRANSL: The water was dragging his body down, slowly, till it came where his mother was.

S.FORM: Viven gis iē, saa sēw roy lē pē, ran̄ ni jējēm ka ni m-mat.
S.TRANSL: Without further ado, she waded through the river to drag him out – thinking he was dead already.

S.FORM: Ni ga ēs woy.
S.TRANSL: In fact he was alive!

S.FORM: Ni m-gal woy viven mēn jarēn.
S.TRANSL: He had just played a trick on his mother.

S.FORM: Jarē Tamat Gēngēn ni ka m-suwaa ni mē.
S.TRANSL: The blood he had covered himself with was that of the Ogress.

S.FORM: Viven mō la mula ni, nōrō van lōk lē qayn̄ēn vat, pas.
S.TRANSL: His mother took him in her arms, and they both walked back to their cave, finally.

S.FORM: Varean.
S.TRANSL: Merci.
Thanks.
